findings.title: Payout bot converts caller-controlled arguments into trusted payout records
findings.description: The page correctly warns that settlement values must be rederived from trusted provider state, but its payout bot does the opposite. An admin-gated function runs as the privileged payout-bot identity and writes args.to and args.amount directly into a protected payouts record under a caller-selected args.id. No trusted settlement record, provider response, immutable entitlement, balance constraint, amount cap, or idempotency condition binds those values. In an application copied from this example, a compromised or over-privileged admin could create fresh payout obligations for an attacker-selected recipient and arbitrary amount, which a downstream settlement worker could treat as authoritative.
findings.recommendation: Accept only a trusted operation identifier, then derive recipient and amount from immutable provider-verified or server-owned settlement state. Make the transition atomic and idempotent, validate identifier shape, and enforce conservation, balance, per-operation, and rolling payout limits with policy invariants.
